Updated assessment incorporating the November 2017 Beige Book:
- Macro: The Beige Book corroborates solid activity through mid-November and a tight labor market, noting notable wage gains in professional, technical, and production roles. Consumer spending was solid in retail and autos, with an upbeat holiday sales outlook. Hurricane rebuilding boosted construction demand and raised materials costs, suggesting some near-term price pressures even as 12‑month inflation remains below 2 percent.
- Policy: Consistent with the FOMC’s December action, the funds rate was raised to 1.25–1.50 percent, policy remains accommodative, the path of hikes is expected to be gradual and below the longer-run rate for some time, and balance-sheet normalization continues.
- Credit/SLOOS: Banks modestly eased some C&I standards amid competition but reported softer business loan demand; consumer credit terms tightened (cards/auto) with softer demand. Net: a mixed-to-slightly softer credit impulse despite solid macro data.
- Financial stability: Elevated valuations and rising business leverage, with core funding risks contained and banks well capitalized—arguing for caution.

Bottom line: Beige Book details on stronger wage momentum and a favorable holiday spending outlook tilt the growth tone a bit more positive than before, but softer credit demand and valuation/leverage risks still warrant a guarded, gradual approach.
